issues.detail: The Hebrew lists Elkanah, his son Ebiasaph, and his son Assir. The Vietnamese renders 'Ê-lê-ka-nah sinh ra Ê-bi-a-sáp, Ê-bi-a-sáp sinh ra A-xia', which makes Elkanah the father of Ebiasaph and Ebiasaph the father of Assir. However, the Hebrew text is a genealogical list of names with 'his son' (בְּנוֹ) repeated, indicating Elkanah is the son of Ebiasaph, and Ebiasaph is the son of Assir (i.e., the order is reversed: Assir → Ebiasaph → Elkanah). The Vietnamese reverses the generational order, making Elkanah the ancestor instead of the descendant, which changes the family relationships.
